title: SCIS has no interface row in TSD S5, no call type, and DP-16 is outside the pattern set of the slice
source: FSD S5 A2.19.2; TSD S5 T5.1 and T-A.1; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 integrations sheet INT-28; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-16
section: s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.9 Call-type summary
description: FEAT-AST-19 submits the vehicle registration transfer through SCIS. The TSD S5 T5.1 external interface table lists INT-11 SVAF, INT-12 AMIS, INT-13 RPS and INT-27 HOME.SCB only, with no SCIS row, and the integration inventory records INT-28 SCIS as Out, approach 'Not available today; prepared by the officer', frequency as needed. No source publishes an operation name, a call type, a file layout or a response shape for the submission, and DP-16 (rwb-integration contract, C RWB-P2-E1007-CON) is not in the pattern set of this slice, which is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19.
evidence: TSD S5 T5.1 rows INT-11 to INT-27; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 line 237 INT-28; FSD S5 A2.19.2 'Integration points. SCIS, RPS'; story row patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 with C [].
proposed: Declare the consumed row as an activity on queue rwb-integration with the placeholder and its gap identifier, build against the adapter document and its fake on Day 1, and let P2 publish the operation name, the call type and the answer shape at the tag of RWB-S5-E4028-CON; no C row is claimed because DP-16 is outside the pattern set.

title: The FSD makes the step a system submission while INT-28 records SCIS as prepared by the officer
source: FSD S5 A1.2 and A2.19; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features and integrations sheets; TSD S5 T6.1
section: s1 Story; s4 Flow; s7 Acceptance criteria; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The feature table of FSD S5 A1.2 gives FEAT-AST-19 the kind System, A2.19.2 describes it as 'Prepares and submits the registration transfer through SCIS', and the features sheet of the Epics 3 to 8 Specification says 'Runs unattended' with SCIS and RPS as systems. The integration inventory records INT-28 SCIS as 'Not available today; prepared by the officer'. No source says whether the Workbench submits the transfer itself once the interface is live, or only prepares the pack that an officer submits, and the legacy story's AC2 says 'registration transferred' without naming the actor.
evidence: FSD S5 A1.2 FEAT-AST-19 row; FSD S5 A2.19.2; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features sheet line 85; integrations sheet line 237; legacy RWB-E4-028 AC2.
proposed: Build the step so that it prepares the pack and submits it through the adapter where the interface answers, and records the officer's submission reference where INT-28 answers 'not available'; both paths sit behind the same activity and the same fixture set, so the answer changes with the interface and not with the code.

title: No element holds the vehicle registration particulars or the SCIS submission reference and its date
source: TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S5 A2.19; legacy RWB-E4-028 Data table
description: The transfer pack needs the registration particulars of the vehicle (registration book number, plate, chassis and engine number) and the SCIS submission reference with its date. TSD S5 T3.1 gives `asset` the columns DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and `asset_sale` the columns DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019; none of them holds a registration particular or a submission reference. The legacy data table names only recovery_case, assignment, v_ace_npa_sale, decision_log_entry and rule_row, and the FSD A2.19 section has no field catalog, unlike A2.20.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset and asset_sale field tables; TSD S5 T3.2 lists; FSD S5 A2.19.3 (no A2.19.3.2 field catalog); legacy RWB-E4-028 Data table.
proposed: Write no column: carry the particulars and the reference with the submission record the decision record holds, and record the gap so that the DB story or the LDM names the element in a later version rather than inventing a column now.

title: R-DIS-53 (transfer rejected, TITLE_BLOCKED) belongs to no story row of the split
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-53; TSD S5 T4; FSD S5 A2.19.4
section: s4 Flow; s5 Exception paths; s9 State transitions; s19 Out of scope
description: The DISPOSAL rule set carries R-DIS-53 from TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING on TRANSFER_REJECTED when SCIS or the Land Office rejects the transfer, to TITLE_BLOCKED, owned by the sale officer with a 5 working day timer. The rule spans the vehicle and the property branch. Legacy RWB-E4-028 has no rejected criterion, its FSD A2.19.4 lists no exception flow for a rejection, and no story row of the split plan names R-DIS-53, so no story owns the state, the task and the timer it raises.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-53; TSD S5 T4 state table (first 25 rows only); FSD S5 A2.19.4.3 exception flows, which name only the role and the decision-log failure; split plan rows for RWB-E4-028.
proposed: Have the branch fail closed on a rejection: nothing moves, the pack and the answer are recorded and an alert is raised, and the state, the task and the timer of R-DIS-53 are allocated to a story of this service in the next split revision; no message is invented for it.

title: The step evaluates the DISPOSAL package while DP-04 is outside the pattern set of the slice
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; story row patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; TSD S5 T4
description: R-DIS-51 is evaluated against the DISPOSAL rule package, which DP-04 governs with H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON. The pattern set of this slice names neither row, and no source says whether the package load is a capability of the service template or a pattern of this slice.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 row; the patterns of RWB-S5-E4028-APP and -CON; FSD S5 A2.19.3.1 rule table.
proposed: Load the package in force through the service template, add no H row for the platform rules kit in this slice, and record the reading so the next revision of the pattern set can confirm it.

title: REQ-S5-008 is claimed by FEAT-AST-08 in the TSD and by FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20 in BR-029
source: TSD S5 T8; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-029; FSD S5 A2.19 and A2.20
description: TSD S5 T8 maps REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only, so REQ-S5-008 is the eviction feature's. BR-029 of the Epic 4 BRD cites REQ-S5-008 for FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20, the vehicle transfer and the Land Office transfer. The split plan carries an empty requirement list for this slice, so the story row does not resolve which claim stands.
evidence: TSD S5 T8 rows REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-08; Epic BRD BR-029 row with REQ-S5-008, FEAT-AST-19, FEAT-AST-20, RWB-E4-028 and RWB-E4-029; story rows with reqs [].
proposed: Trace the slice to BR-029 and name REQ-S5-008 with the collision stated, allocate the next free REQ-S5 id to FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20 when the PRD of S5 is drafted, and leave the PRD reference as Pending (C1).
